# Property taxes

**Cambridge's property tax levy — the total amount of property tax the district collects — rose from about $8.2 million in 2014–15 to $10.1 million in 2025–26, an increase of about 23%. Consumer prices rose about 38% over the same years, so after adjusting for inflation the levy is about 11% lower than it was in 2014–15.**

The chart below shows each district's levy since 2014–15 in inflation-adjusted dollars (2024–25 dollars; see [Methods](../appendix/methods.qmd) for the adjustment), with nearby districts for context.

```{python}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())

import polars as pl
from plotnine import (
    aes,
    geom_line,
    geom_point,
    ggplot,
    labs,
    scale_color_manual,
    scale_x_continuous,
    scale_y_continuous,
)
from great_tables import GT, loc, md, style

import comparisons as cc

# Find repo root to locate data (works from Jupyter context)
def _find_repo_root():
    cwd = Path.cwd()
    for base in [cwd, *cwd.parents][:5]:
        if (base / "data" / "crosswalks").is_dir():
            return base
    raise FileNotFoundError("Could not find repo root")

REPO_ROOT = _find_repo_root()
PROCESSED_DIR = REPO_ROOT / "data" / "processed"

# Years shown: the first and latest years in the Comptroller's levy data.
# Dollar amounts are shown in inflation-adjusted (2024-25) dollars.
FIRST_YEAR, LAST_YEAR = 2015, 2026
SPAN = f"{cc.school_year_label(FIRST_YEAR)} to {cc.school_year_label(LAST_YEAR)}"
YEARS_CAPTION = (
    f"{FIRST_YEAR} ({cc.school_year_label(FIRST_YEAR)}) through "
    f"{LAST_YEAR} ({cc.school_year_label(LAST_YEAR)})"
)

# OSC data uses nysed_district_cd; load and join to comparison groups
osc = pl.read_parquet(PROCESSED_DIR / "osc_school_district_tax_levies.parquet")
osc_totals = osc.filter(pl.col("record_type") == "district_total")

def tax_levy_for(group: dict[str, str]) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Levy, taxable full value and tax rate for group, labelled like other
    panels, with the dollar amounts also in inflation-adjusted dollars."""
    region_by_cd = {
        cd: ("Washington County" if cd in cc.WASHINGTON_K12 else "Other comparison districts")
        for cd in group
    }
    return (
        osc_totals.filter(pl.col("nysed_district_cd").is_in(list(group)))
        .with_columns(
            pl.col("nysed_district_cd").replace_strict(group).alias("district"),
            pl.col("nysed_district_cd").replace_strict(region_by_cd).alias("region"),
        )
        .select(
            "district", "region", "year_end",
            "tax_levy", "taxable_full_value", "full_value_tax_rate",
        )
        .filter(pl.col("year_end").is_between(FIRST_YEAR, LAST_YEAR))
        .pipe(cc.to_real, ["tax_levy", "taxable_full_value"])
        .with_columns(
            (pl.col("tax_levy") / 1_000_000).alias("levy_millions"),
            (pl.col("tax_levy_real") / 1_000_000).alias("levy_real_millions"),
        )
        .sort("district", "year_end")
    )


tax = tax_levy_for(cc.GRAPH_GROUP)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Checks on the statements made in the text of this chapter. If the data
# change so that a statement is no longer true, the page fails to build
# instead of quietly showing text that disagrees with its own charts.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def _by_district(col, year_end):
    rows = tax.filter(pl.col("year_end") == year_end)
    return dict(zip(rows["district"], rows[col]))


def _pct(col):
    a, b = _by_district(col, FIRST_YEAR), _by_district(col, LAST_YEAR)
    return {d: 100 * (b[d] / a[d] - 1) for d in b}


_cam = tax.filter(pl.col("district") == cc.FOCUS).sort("year_end")
_cam_by_year = {r["year_end"]: r for r in _cam.iter_rows(named=True)}
_c0, _c1 = _cam_by_year[FIRST_YEAR], _cam_by_year[LAST_YEAR]

# Cambridge's levy, before and after adjusting for inflation.
assert round(_c0["levy_millions"], 1) == 8.2 and round(_c1["levy_millions"], 1) == 10.1
assert round(_pct("tax_levy")[cc.FOCUS]) == 23
assert round(_c0["levy_real_millions"], 1) == 11.0
assert round(_c1["levy_real_millions"], 1) == 9.8
assert round(_pct("tax_levy_real")[cc.FOCUS]) == -11
_px = cc.load_price_index()
_idx = dict(zip(_px["year_end"], _px["index_value"]))
assert round(100 * (_idx[LAST_YEAR] / _idx[FIRST_YEAR] - 1)) == 38

# Cambridge's levy rose every year before adjusting for inflation. After
# adjusting, it stayed between $10.9 and $11.2 million through 2020-21 and
# has been below $10 million since 2022-23.
assert _cam["tax_levy"].diff().drop_nulls().min() > 0
_early = _cam.filter(pl.col("year_end") <= 2021)["levy_real_millions"]
assert 10.9 <= _early.min() and _early.max() <= 11.2
assert _cam.filter(pl.col("year_end") >= 2023)["levy_real_millions"].max() < 10.0

# The five districts: every levy is lower after inflation; Greenwich fell
# least, then Cambridge; Hoosick Falls and Salem fell most.
_real_pct = _pct("tax_levy_real")
assert all(v < 0 for v in _real_pct.values())
assert sorted(_real_pct, key=_real_pct.get, reverse=True)[:2] == ["Greenwich", cc.FOCUS]
assert round(_real_pct["Greenwich"]) == -8
assert round(_real_pct["Hoosick Falls"]) == -19 and round(_real_pct["Salem"]) == -20

# Taxable full value (the tax base), before adjusting for inflation.
_fv = {y: r["taxable_full_value"] / 1e6 for y, r in _cam_by_year.items()}
assert all(500 <= _fv[y] <= 521 for y in range(FIRST_YEAR, 2023))
assert round(100 * (_fv[2023] / _fv[2022] - 1)) == 24
assert round(_fv[LAST_YEAR]) == 813
assert round(_pct("taxable_full_value")[cc.FOCUS]) == 61
# ...and it jumped in every one of the five districts in 2022-23.
for _d in cc.GRAPH_GROUP.values():
    _r = tax.filter(pl.col("district") == _d).sort("year_end")
    _g = dict(zip(_r["year_end"], _r["taxable_full_value"].pct_change()))
    assert _g[2023] > 0.12, _d

# Full-value tax rate.
_rate = {y: r["full_value_tax_rate"] for y, r in _cam_by_year.items()}
assert all(16.3 <= _rate[y] <= 17.95 for y in range(FIRST_YEAR, 2023))
assert [round(_rate[y], 1) for y in range(2023, 2027)] == [14.8, 13.8, 13.0, 12.5]
assert round(_rate[FIRST_YEAR], 2) == 16.32 and round(_rate[LAST_YEAR], 2) == 12.46
_r0, _r1 = (_by_district("full_value_tax_rate", y) for y in (FIRST_YEAR, LAST_YEAR))
_rate_chg = {d: _r1[d] - _r0[d] for d in _r1}
assert round(_rate_chg[cc.FOCUS], 2) == -3.86
assert all(v < 0 for v in _rate_chg.values())
assert max(_rate_chg, key=_rate_chg.get) == cc.FOCUS          # smallest decline
assert min(_rate_chg, key=_rate_chg.get) == "Schuylerville"   # largest decline
assert round(_rate_chg["Schuylerville"], 1) == -8.0
assert sorted(_r0, key=_r0.get).index(cc.FOCUS) == 1          # 2nd lowest of 5
assert sorted(_r1, key=_r1.get).index(cc.FOCUS) == 2          # 3rd lowest of 5
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-tax-levy
#| fig-cap: "School district property tax levy by school year ending, 2015 (2014–15) through 2026 (2025–26), in millions of inflation-adjusted (2024–25) dollars. Source: NYS Comptroller local-government data (Table 3); U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Consumer Price Index (CPI-U)."
g = tax
cambridge = g.filter(pl.col("district") == cc.FOCUS)

(
    ggplot(g, aes("year_end", "levy_real_millions", color="district"))
    + geom_line(size=1)
    + geom_point(size=1.8)
    + geom_line(cambridge, size=2.4)  # emphasize the focus district
    + scale_color_manual(
        values=cc.PALETTE, name="", limits=cc.district_order(cc.GRAPH_GROUP)
    )
    + scale_x_continuous(breaks=list(range(FIRST_YEAR, LAST_YEAR + 1)))
    + labs(
        x="School year ending",
        y="Tax levy (millions of 2024–25 dollars)",
        title=f"Property tax levy after inflation, {SPAN}",
    )
    + cc.theme_ccs()
)
```

Before adjusting for inflation, Cambridge's levy rose every year. After adjusting, it stayed close to $11 million through 2020–21, fell when prices rose quickly in 2021–22 and 2022–23, and has been a little under $10 million since.

The same thing happened in all five districts: each one's levy grew more slowly than prices. Greenwich's levy lost the least ground to inflation (about 8%), followed by Cambridge (about 11%). Hoosick Falls and Salem lost the most (about 19% and 20%).

```{python}
#| label: tbl-tax-levy-change
#| tbl-cap: "Property tax levy in 2014–15 and 2025–26, in inflation-adjusted (2024–25) dollars, with change before and after adjusting for inflation, by district."
ends = tax.filter(pl.col("year_end").is_in([FIRST_YEAR, LAST_YEAR])).sort("district", "year_end")
levy_wide = (
    ends.group_by("region", "district", maintain_order=True)
    .agg(
        real_first=pl.col("levy_real_millions").first(),
        real_last=pl.col("levy_real_millions").last(),
        pct_real=pl.col("tax_levy_real").last() / pl.col("tax_levy_real").first() - 1,
        pct_nominal=pl.col("tax_levy").last() / pl.col("tax_levy").first() - 1,
    )
    .with_columns(
        pl.when(pl.col("region") == "Washington County").then(0).otherwise(1).alias("_rank")
    )
    .sort(["_rank", "district"])
    .drop("_rank")
)

(
    GT(levy_wide, rowname_col="district", groupname_col="region")
    .tab_header(
        title="Property tax levy",
        subtitle=f"{SPAN}, millions of inflation-adjusted (2024–25) dollars",
    )
    .fmt_currency(columns=["real_first", "real_last"], decimals=1, pattern="{x}M")
    .fmt_percent(columns=["pct_real", "pct_nominal"], decimals=0, force_sign=True)
    .tab_spanner(label="Levy, 2024–25 dollars", columns=["real_first", "real_last"])
    .tab_spanner(label="Change", columns=["pct_real", "pct_nominal"])
    .cols_label(
        real_first=cc.school_year_label(FIRST_YEAR),
        real_last=cc.school_year_label(LAST_YEAR),
        pct_real=md("After<br>inflation"),
        pct_nominal=md("Before<br>inflation"),
    )
    .tab_style(
        style=[style.fill(color="#FCEFB4"), style.text(weight="bold")],
        locations=[
            loc.body(rows=pl.col("district") == cc.FOCUS),
            loc.stub(rows=pl.col("district") == cc.FOCUS),
        ],
    )
    .tab_source_note(
        md(
            "**Source:** NYS Comptroller local-government data, Table 3. Adjusted "
            "for inflation with the Consumer Price Index (CPI-U), averaged over "
            "each school year. \"Before inflation\" compares the dollar amounts "
            "as levied."
        )
    )
)
```

## The tax rate: what property owners pay per value

The **levy** is what the district collects. The **full-value tax rate** is what property owners pay per $1,000 of taxable full value — the standard way to compare tax effort across places with different assessment practices.

A higher tax rate means property owners pay more for each dollar of property value. The chart below shows how Cambridge's full-value tax rate has changed since 2014–15. A rate is a ratio of two dollar amounts, so it needs no inflation adjustment.

```{python}
#| label: fig-tax-rate
#| fig-cap: "Full-value tax rate by school year ending, 2015 (2014–15) through 2026 (2025–26). The rate is the levy per $1,000 of taxable full value. Source: NYS Comptroller local-government data (Table 3)."
g = tax
cambridge = g.filter(pl.col("district") == cc.FOCUS)

(
    ggplot(g, aes("year_end", "full_value_tax_rate", color="district"))
    + geom_line(size=1)
    + geom_point(size=1.8)
    + geom_line(cambridge, size=2.4)  # emphasize the focus district
    + scale_color_manual(
        values=cc.PALETTE, name="", limits=cc.district_order(cc.GRAPH_GROUP)
    )
    + scale_x_continuous(breaks=list(range(FIRST_YEAR, LAST_YEAR + 1)))
    + labs(
        x="School year ending",
        y="Full-value tax rate (per $1,000)",
        title=f"Full-value property tax rate, {SPAN}",
    )
    + cc.theme_ccs()
)
```

Cambridge's tax rate stayed between about $16 and $18 per $1,000 of full value through 2021–22, then **fell every year after that** — to about $14.8 in 2022–23 and $12.5 in 2025–26. The drop coincides with a **jump in taxable full value** (the tax base). Full value is the state's estimate of what taxable property is worth on the market. Cambridge's was between $500 million and $520 million every year through 2021–22, rose 24% in 2022–23, and reached $813 million in 2025–26. Full value jumped in all five districts in 2022–23, which points to rising property values across the area and not to anything particular to Cambridge.

The table below shows where each district stood in 2014–15 and 2025–26, and how much their tax rates changed.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-tax-rate-change
#| tbl-cap: "Full-value tax rate in 2014–15 and 2025–26, with change, by district."
g = tax.select("district", "region", "year_end", "full_value_tax_rate").filter(
    pl.col("year_end").is_in([FIRST_YEAR, LAST_YEAR])
)
y0, y1 = str(FIRST_YEAR), str(LAST_YEAR)

wide = (
    g.with_columns(
        pl.when(pl.col("region") == "Washington County").then(0).otherwise(1).alias("_rank")
    )
    .pivot(values="full_value_tax_rate", index=["_rank", "region", "district"], on="year_end")
    .sort(["_rank", "district"])
    .drop("_rank")
)

wide = wide.with_columns((pl.col(y1) - pl.col(y0)).alias("change"))

(
    GT(wide, rowname_col="district", groupname_col="region")
    .tab_header(
        title="Full-value property tax rate",
        subtitle=f"School-year-ending {YEARS_CAPTION.replace(' through ', ' and ')}, per $1,000",
    )
    .fmt_number(columns=[y0, y1, "change"], decimals=2)
    .tab_spanner(label="School year ending", columns=[y0, y1])
    .cols_label(change=md(f"Change<br>{y0}→{y1}"))
    .tab_style(
        style=[style.fill(color="#FCEFB4"), style.text(weight="bold")],
        locations=[
            loc.body(rows=pl.col("district") == cc.FOCUS),
            loc.stub(rows=pl.col("district") == cc.FOCUS),
        ],
    )
    .tab_source_note(
        md(
            "**Source:** NYS Comptroller local-government data, Table 3 (school "
            "district tax levies, taxable full value, and full-value tax rates). "
            "Rate = levy ÷ taxable full value × 1,000. Year = school-year-ending "
            "(2026 = 2025–26)."
        )
    )
)
```

**Cambridge's tax rate fell by $3.86 per $1,000** between 2014–15 and 2025–26 (from $16.32 to $12.46). Rates fell in all five districts; Cambridge's decline was the smallest of the five and Schuylerville's (about $8.00) the largest. Cambridge had the second-lowest rate of the five in 2014–15 and the third-lowest in 2025–26. The rates fell because the tax base grew faster than the levy: Cambridge's full value rose about 61% while its levy rose about 23%.

## What this means for Cambridge

The tax story has two parts:

- **The levy (what Cambridge collects)** has risen 23% since 2014–15, to $10.1 million — less than the 38% rise in consumer prices. [CLAUDE: Both facts are true: up 23% in dollars, down 11% after inflation. The lead gives both. Your call on which one this summary stresses.] This funds the district's operations — the same spending per pupil discussed in the [Spending](spending.qmd) chapter.
- **The rate (what property owners pay)** has fallen recently as property values rose, which could provide relief to property owners even as the levy continues to climb. [CLAUDE: A lower rate does not mean a lower bill. The rate fell because values rose. If every property's value rises by the same share, each owner's bill moves with the levy and not with the rate. Bills fall only for owners whose property rose in value less than average. I would cut "relief".]

The underlying pressure is the same: Cambridge's declining enrollment (see the [Enrollment](enrollment.qmd) chapter) means fewer taxpayers to spread the levy across, even as fixed costs remain. The district's low students-per-teacher ratio (see the [Students per teacher](students-per-teacher.qmd) chapter) adds spending pressure, which ultimately feeds back into what the levy must collect.

[CLAUDE: Students are not taxpayers. Enrollment fell 18% while the tax base grew 61%, and we have no count of taxpayers or households in the data. I would cut "fewer taxpayers". What the finance chapters show together is this: from 2015–16 to 2024–25 total operating spending fell about 4% after inflation, the levy fell about 11%, and Foundation Aid fell about 7%, while enrollment fell 14%. Somewhat fewer real dollars, spread over many fewer students. I think that is the summary this section should give.]

*Data sources:*
- **NYS Comptroller** school-district tax levies, taxable full value, and full-value rates, 2014–15 through 2025–26
- **U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics** Consumer Price Index (CPI-U), for the inflation adjustment
